page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the n2 family. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of dedicated RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results place the n2-highmem-8 in the average performance tier for most multi-core and memory-bound operations. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is positioned in the bottom 25%, while multi-core performance falls in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth tests, including read-only and write operations on large blocks, consistently register average throughput. The instance demonstrates average performance in database operations, static web serving, and Redis SET operations, but exhibits weaker performance in compute-heavy tasks such as ray tracing, image processing, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Large language model inference speeds are weak to poor, particularly for medium-sized models.

Given its high memory density relative to compute resources, the n2-highmem-8 offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require substantial RAM without demanding top-tier CPU performance. The dedicated CPU allocation and 33 MB L3 cache support stable execution of memory-intensive applications. This hardware profile is suited for database hosting, in-memory caching systems like Redis, text processing pipelines, and general-purpose enterprise applications that require a balanced memory-to-core ratio.
